subject: VAT registration triggers for co-sell marketplace listings — who must register / invoicing implications
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Subject: Clarify: EU VAT registration thresholds + marketplace co-sell billing question

Team —

Acme (cc'ed below via contracts@acme-retail.com) called with a scenario that surfaced two intertwined questions and I want a single, clear response we can send to them and to AWS Marketplace Support:

1) If Acme moves to a co-sell listing where the customer is billed through AWS (marketplace flow), at what point (country-specific thresholds) does Redwood or the reseller need to register for VAT in the buyer"s country? Who is legally responsible for VAT registration under:
   - AWS seller-of-record (SOR) configurations
   - Marketplace reseller / distributor arrangements

2) For US entities buying via marketplace, we need to confirm when we request W-9 vs W-8 (for US vs non-US vendors) from the buyer or reseller, and whether marketplace consolidated billing changes our data/collection obligations.

Attached a quick spreadsheet I pulled together with EU thresholds by country — I modeled it fast (eu-vat-thresholds.xlsx). Can you: (a) correct any errors, (b) give a short paragraph we can send to Acme explaining which party is typically the registrant in each marketplace model, and (c) list the specific documents we should request from Acme (W-9 / W-8BEN-E / VAT registration certs / EORI) depending on their corporate structure?

Need to send a coherent reply by end of day so Acme can proceed with procurement. Thanks —

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks Hannah — good, concrete ask. High-level summary we should send to Acme, and a couple of operational notes. See inline.

(Attachment: mktplace-role-matrix.pdf)

Short explanatory paragraph for the customer (suggested):
"In marketplace transactions the party responsible for VAT depends on marketplace configuration and the customer's status. For AWS/Azure/GCP there are two common flows: (1) Seller-of-record (SOR) where the marketplace or reseller is the invoice/collection entity — in that case the marketplace/reseller typically handles VAT collection and filings for sales they invoice; (2) Direct billing (seller-billed) or customer-billed models where Redwood invoices the end customer directly — the end customer is then responsible for local VAT obligations where applicable. For B2B purchases in the EU where the buyer has a valid VAT number, reverse charge may apply (buyer accounts for VAT), but the buyer must provide a valid VAT registration number for that to be valid."

Operational items and who to involve: 
- AWS Marketplace SOR: confirm with AWS whether this listing would be SOR. If SOR = AWS/reseller issues invoice, AWS"s marketplace settlements team will provide invoice copies and (in many cases) take on VAT collection for sales they invoice. We still need to ensure tax evidence is captured (VAT numbers, business status).
- Reseller vs Distributor: resellers in EU sometimes act as SOR or perform rebill. If Redwood is not SOR, we may still have obligations around reporting and helping the customer with evidence.
- W-8 / W-9: request a W-9 from any US billing entity. For non-US entities, request the appropriate W-8BEN-E classification for US-source payments. Those documents are only relevant for US tax withholding — they don"t substitute for EU VAT evidence.

Suggested ask to Acme (concise list we can send):
1) Confirm billing entity (legal name and tax residence).
2) Provide VAT registration number(s) for any EU entity that will be buying.
3) If billing entity is US-based, provide W-9. If non-US and receiving US-source payments, provide W-8BEN-E.
4) Estimate annual spend via marketplace + per-country split if possible (this helps assess registration triggers).

I"ll tidy the language and we should include the matrix PDF that maps SOR/reseller behaviors by cloud marketplace. Vanessa

Hannah — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifying Qs from our side so we can loop in procurement: 
1) Are there hard thresholds per country we should be looking at (i.e., €10k/€35k/etc.) or does it vary materially?
2) If our UK entity buys via AWS Marketplace SOR and we are VAT-registered in the UK, do we still need to provide anything else to Redwood or AWS?
3) If Redwood helps coordinate registrations in small EU countries (e.g., Estonia, Lithuania), will that impact our ability to reclaim VAT?

We can provide spend estimates but want to understand whether Redwood or the marketplace will front filings and whether that changes the tax reclaim process for us.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: VAT registration triggers for co-sell marketplace listings — who must register / invoicing implications

Thanks — answered inline and added a short country-level guidance + next steps. (Attachment: eu-threshold-summary.pdf)

1) Thresholds: there is no single pan-EU threshold any more; each member state sets its own registration threshold for domestic sales. For distance sales and OSS/MOSS rules, the EU changed the landscape in recent years so many low thresholds were harmonized under OSS but there are still differences for B2C vs B2B. Practical guidance: if estimated annual taxable sales to a single EU country via the marketplace exceed that country's distance-sell threshold (or if the marketplace is acting as SOR for that country), the party invoicing that customer will generally be responsible for VAT registration/collection in that country. See attached summary for common thresholds we encounter.

2) UK-specific: UK left the EU VAT regime — the UK has its own registration thresholds. If your UK legal entity is buying and is VAT-registered, you should provide your VAT number; reverse charge can apply if the invoice is made to your UK VAT-registered entity and the supplier is outside the UK, but marketplace/SOR arrangements change the flow. If AWS invoices your UK entity directly (SOR), AWS will handle VAT on their invoices; you will receive AWS invoice and reclaim per normal UK reclaim rules. You still should provide your VAT number so the correct treatment can be applied.

3) Reclaimability: if Redwood or the marketplace registers and collects VAT for sales, Acme"s reclaim process stays consistent — you reclaim against the VAT you paid on the supplier invoice, provided you have valid tax invoices and the payments were VAT-charged properly. If Redwood assists with registration and is the entity charging VAT, we will issue compliant VAT invoices so reclaim should be possible. We do recommend keeping legal entity mappings clear (which entity paid which invoice) so treasury/procurement can do reclaim exercises.

Proposed next steps (Mutual Action Plan):
- Acme: provide billing entity details + estimated monthly spend by country (we can accept ranges).
- Redwood: confirm whether the proposed marketplace listing will be SOR or non-SOR with AWS (we will open a case with AWS Marketplace Support and loop them in).
- If SOR or reseller re-bill is likely and estimates exceed local thresholds, Redwood can offer a managed registration path (we"ve done this for customers on Dedicated/DSP) — we will provide a scope and cost estimate.

I"ve attached a short country table and included links to relevant EU OSS guidance in the attachment. Happy to set a 30-min call to walk Acme and procurement through this next week.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Acme / team — thanks for the questions and the details. Quick summary and concrete asks to move procurement forward: 

Summary (one-liner for procurement): if the marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) or a reseller is the invoice issuer (SOR), they typically handle VAT collection and filing for the sales they invoice. If Redwood is the invoicing party, Redwood (or the buyer) is typically responsible for local VAT registration and filings. For B2B transactions with a valid EU VAT number, reverse charge may apply but the buyer must supply that VAT number at purchase.

What we need from Acme (please send these to contracts@acme-retail.com):
- Confirm the legal billing entity name and country of registration.
- Provide VAT registration numbers for any EU entities (if applicable).
- If US-based billing entity: provide a completed W-9. If non-US and applicable for US withholding: provide W-8BEN-E.
- Share estimated monthly marketplace spend and an approximate country split if possible (this helps us determine registration triggers).

Next steps from Redwood:
- We will open a case with AWS Marketplace Support to confirm SOR vs reseller rebill for the proposed listing and share the SOR decision + sample invoice flow.
- If registration looks necessary and Acme wants Redwood to assist, we will provide a scoped quote for managed registration and invoicing support.

I"ve attached the country threshold summary and our marketplace role matrix. Karthik — can you draft a 15-minute deck we can share with Acme procurement and schedule a follow-up for next Wednesday?

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
